source.title: Why Do Aligned LLMs Remain Jailbreakable: Refusal-Escape Directions, Operator-Level Sources, and Safety-Utility Trade-off
source.authors: Yu Chen; Yuan-Hao Liu; Qian Cao

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites and discusses work on refusal directions, but its experiments analyze a distinct, pair-specific Refusal-Escape Direction (RED). They do not test the difference-in-means direction from the claim by removing or adding it, or otherwise measure the claim versions’ named mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own RED and jailbreak-transition results, but these concern a different, pair-specific construction rather than the claim’s difference-in-means refusal direction. The figures’ numerical values are not stated in the text; qualitative descriptions are recorded below. The paper also cites prior findings, which are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. only in related work and as one possible proxy for a target-behavior subspace. Its experiments use a pair-specific harmful–jailbreak logit-difference direction and a Jacobian-based Refusal-Escape Direction, not the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. It never ablates or adds any direction and never measures refusal rates under intervention. Its jailbreak analysis (V3-adjacent) measures alignment with its own RED construct, not suppression of the claim's direction. So no row bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors also present a theoretical result: exactly eliminating RED conditionally conflicts with benign behavior (a safety–utility trade-off, Theorem 1). The paraphrase omits this; it is a proof, not an empirical result.
record.recipe_differences: The paper constructs a pair-specific reference direction from a harmful–jailbreak final-token logit contrast and a reference harmful-semantics subspace from clean-input sensitivity. It analyzes input transformations and operator contributions, rather than using the original study’s harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction and all-layer, all-position ablation/addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary with attack method and model: GCG progress is more dispersed; Qwen3-4B/14B often show successful judgments within the first 5%, while Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B/12B-IT typically show them later, often between 20% and 60%. The reference construction is pair-specific and uses placeholder padding and a linear interpolation between aligned prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the paper's construction, zero-embedding placeholder padding makes the pair-specific RED nonzero at harmful inputs. The terminal-source contribution is the most stable and prominent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Added token dimensions expose semantics-preserving directions that steer answer-versus-refusal logits, with a prominent terminal-source side-channel.

fits_no_version.finding: Along interpolations from harmful to jailbreak prompts, the local behavior change is mostly accounted for by RED (ratio near 1), and terminal-source contributions are most consistently positive. Qwen3 models flip earlier (often within the first 5%) than Llama and Gemma (often 20–60%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Successful jailbreak transitions align with a pair-specific refusal-escape direction; model vulnerability to local perturbation varies by family.

record.problems: The experiments use pair-specific reference choices that the authors say are a controlled instantiation rather than the only possible empirical realization. The harmful-semantics-preserving interpretation is local and first-order. The authors note that causal validation should be strengthened with failed attacks and benign transformations and by testing whether RED suppression reduces jailbreak success. The main quantitative plots are not numerically described in the text, and uncertainty estimates are not stated. No general-capability check is reported.
record.rows_left_out: The figures contain additional model-specific and attack-specific distributions and source-alignment plots, but the text does not state their numerical values. Rows retain the qualitative outcomes explicitly described in Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendix E.2.1–E.2.2; individual unreported plot values were not transcribed.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction, no ablation or addition, no capability check.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the difference-in-means direction, and does no adversarial training against its ablation; it analyzes only its own pair-specific RED.
The operator-source decomposition is of RED, not a test of a refusal cone or affine structure.
It assumes rather than measures a separation between harmful-semantics sensitivity and refusal; no separate measures are reported.
No reasoning-mode condition; Qwen3 is not examined as a reasoning model.

record.verdict_notes: Mostly theoretical. The ratio near 1 is partly expected by construction, because the semantic subspace is defined from the same target sensitivity at the clean input; the authors acknowledge that causal validation is lacking. Results are figure-only with no numbers or uncertainty, and the judge is Qwen3Guard refusal parsing. There is no relevance to the difference-in-means refusal direction beyond citation.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found or causally ablated or added; no general-capability effect is measured.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is performed.
The paper analyzes jailbreak transitions relative to its own RED, but does not test whether attacks suppress the claim’s direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The operator-source decomposition concerns the paper’s RED construction; it does not test whether the claim’s refusal direction is affine, conic, or accompanied by other refusal directions.
No separate empirical measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
The paper compares models and attacks but does not test transfer of the claim’s direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No training procedure, timing, or stage is varied to test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.
